tagline: Empowering physicians with technology to identify, manage, and treat chronic diseases earlier
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of Medicare Advantage members is the primary driver of growth and scalability for the Clover Assistant platform, as more members generate more data to fuel clinical AI models.

kpis.name: Number of members
kpis.explanation: Total number of beneficiaries enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans at the end of the period.
kpis.description: Membership is a key indicator of market penetration and the data foundation for clinical AI. As of end-2025, 113,803 members were enrolled.
kpis.signal: Fast growth of 53% YoY announced for 2026

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue from insurance premiums and other sources.
kpis.description: Revenue primarily comes from Medicare Advantage insurance premiums. In 2025, revenue reached $1,924.3M.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth driven by membership expansion and premium increases

kpis.name: Medical Expense Ratio (BER)
kpis.explanation: Ratio of net medical expenses to premiums earned, indicating medical cost efficiency.
kpis.description: BER increased significantly in 2025, reflecting pressure on medical costs or poor risk anticipation.
kpis.signal: Deterioration in BER in 2025, rising from 81.2% to 90.9%

kpis.name: Normalized BER
kpis.explanation: BER adjusted to exclude certain non-recurring impacts, providing a more stable view of medical costs.
kpis.description: Normalized BER is slightly higher than gross BER, indicating stable management of adjustments.
kpis.signal: Normalized BER follows the same negative trend, confirming margin pressure

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, and non-recurring adjustments.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA declined from $70.1M in 2024 to $21.7M in 2025, reflecting pressure on operating margins.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in Adjusted EBITDA in 2025 despite revenue growth

kpis.name: Net loss
kpis.explanation: Annual net loss after all expenses.
kpis.description: Net loss improved from $210.1M in 2023 to $46.3M in 2024, then widened to $85.5M in 2025, showing improvement followed by deterioration.
kpis.signal: Significant reduction in net loss in 2025 compared to 2024

risks.title: Repeated net losses and uncertain profitability
risks.score_rationale: The risk is listed first in the document and cites significant losses over multiple years with an accumulated deficit of $2.3B. The language emphasizes uncertainty around future profitability. The 'Capital' category is heavily weighted here due to financial viability concerns. Its central placement in the 10-K and strong language ('may not be able to achieve or maintain profitability') justify maximum severity.

risks.title: Potential failure of SaaS Counterpart Assistant launch
risks.score_rationale: The launch of Counterpart Health is described as strategic but with high uncertainty regarding adoption, costs, and execution. Repeated mentions across sections with concerning language ('may not be successful', 'could harm our reputation'). An existential risk due to its link to economic model diversification. High placement in the document and product novelty justify high severity.

risks.title: Difficulty in physician adoption of Clover Assistant
risks.score_rationale: Multiple paragraphs detail adoption barriers (EHR integration, perception, training, competition). Repetitive and concerning language ('decline in lives under management', 'frustrating experience'). This risk is central because the entire model's effectiveness depends on prescriber usage. The 'Technology' category is moderately weighted, but operational impact is high.

risks.title: Poor control over medical costs (MCR)
risks.score_rationale: The risk is flagged as critical to profitability ('profitability could decline'). Depends on external factors (inflation, regulation) and internal capabilities (AI adoption, care management). Strong language ('materially and adversely affect'). Directly tied to the health insurance business model. Key placement in the document and direct impact on cash flows justify maximum severity.

risks.title: Risk of non-compliance with healthcare regulations
risks.score_rationale: Multiple references to risks related to health data privacy (HIPAA, CMS) and regulatory requirements. Concerning language ('significant liability', 'reputational harm'). SaaS expansion increases exposure. While not framed as existential, regulatory impact could be severe. The 'Regulation' category is moderately weighted, but the healthcare context is sensitive.

risks.title: Dependence on elderly enrollee retention
risks.score_rationale: The document stresses that long-term value depends on retaining elderly members. If patients leave, preventive care investments are not recouped. Explicit language ('we would not be compensated'). Direct impact on clinical program profitability. The 'Industrial' category is moderately weighted, but this is a strong structural risk.

ai_positioning.summary: Clover Assistant is positioned as a core element of the company's strategy, a proprietary cloud platform that uses machine learning models to deliver personalized, data-driven recommendations to physicians at the point of care.
evidence: Clover Assistant (licensed externally as Counterpart Assistant) supports clinical real-time decision making at the point of care by equipping the clinical with data and insights
cloud-based software platform that curates data from over 100 sources and provides physicians with access to data-driven insights and personalized care recommendations
use and continuous improvement of Clover Assistant has resulted in not only improved clinical decision-making but also enhanced MA plan performance
The platform facilitates identifying and engaging with our most at-risk members for our clinical programs
